title_en: Canons of the Council of Laodicea
author: Council of Laodicea
occasion: The source presents a series of disciplinary and liturgical canons with later explanatory commentary, but gives no narrative introduction stating who issued them, to whom, or why.
argument: The canons regulate reconciliation of the twice-married and penitent sinners to communion, bar the newly baptized from ordination, and forbid priests from lending at interest. They exclude heretics from churches and mixed marriages, and require returning heretics to be catechized, chrismated, or baptized as appropriate. They set rules for worship, including who may sing, read, or enter the sanctuary, and require the same liturgy of prayers at the ninth hour and at vespers. They forbid Christians from Judaizing, attending heretical or pagan festivals, magic, and lax conduct at weddings. They impose Lenten fasting discipline, limit baptismal preparation, and close with a list of the canonical books of the Old and New Testaments.

outline.move: Rules for reconciling the twice-married and penitent sinners to communion.
Rules against ordaining the newly baptized, priests lending at interest, and ordinations in the presence of hearers.
Rules excluding heretics from churches and regulating the reception of Novatians, Photinians, Quartodecimans, and Phrygians, and forbidding visits to heretical shrines and marriages with heretics.
Rules against appointing women elders and regulating episcopal elections by bishops rather than crowds.
Rules for sending the Eucharist at Pascha, who may sing and read in church, and the order of prayers in the liturgy.

Rules on seating and duties of deacons, servants, readers, singers, exorcists, and doorkeepers, and against those in ecclesiastical orders from presbyters to ascetics entering taverns or taking portions at love feasts.

Rules forbidding Judaizing, bathing with women, marriages with heretics, receiving heretical blessings, praying with heretics or schismatics, honoring false martyrs, invoking angels, magic, and sharing in Jewish or pagan festivals.
Rules requiring bishops to attend synods and clergy to travel only with the bishop's permission and canonical letters.
Rule barring women from entering the sanctuary.
Rules regulating baptismal preparation, instruction in the faith, and chrismation.
Rules for Lent: no bread offerings except Saturday and Sunday, no breaking the fast on Thursday of the last week, no martyr festivals, marriages, or birthday celebrations.
Rules forbidding dancing at weddings and clergy attending spectacles or contributing to banquets.

Rules on presbyters entering the sanctuary, rural bishops and presbyters acting only with the city bishop's consent, no offerings in private houses, and no private psalms or uncanonical books in church.
List of the canonical books of the Old and New Testaments to be read in church.

cast.name: Bishops
cast.who: Overseers of city churches who ordain, judge, and govern.

cast.name: Presbyters
cast.who: Elders serving under bishops in teaching, baptizing, and offering.

cast.name: Deacons
cast.who: Ministers ranked below presbyters with liturgical and service duties.

cast.name: Servants
cast.who: Attendants who guard doors and handle vessels but may not bless or distribute; later tradition identifies them with subdeacons.

cast.name: Readers
cast.who: Those appointed to read Scripture in church.

cast.name: Singers
cast.who: Canonical cantors who chant from the ambo.

cast.name: Exorcists
cast.who: Those appointed by bishops to exorcise.

cast.name: Ascetics
cast.who: Those belonging to the order of ascetics, mentioned only as forbidden to enter taverns.

cast.name: Hearers
cast.who: Those present and listening at an ordination; the source does not define them as a technical class.

cast.name: Penitents
cast.who: Those undergoing penance before readmission to communion.

cast.name: Photinians
cast.who: Followers of Photinus, regarded as heretics.

cast.name: Quartodecimans
cast.who: Those who observed Pascha on the fourteenth of Nisan.

cast.name: Phrygians
cast.who: Montanists, a prophetic sect requiring rebaptism.

cast.name: Jews
cast.who: Non-Christian Jews whose festivals and unleavened bread are forbidden to Christians.

cast.name: Pagans
cast.who: Non-Christian Gentiles whose festivals Christians must avoid.

voices.speaker: Council of Laodicea
voices.how_marked: The canons are the council's own decrees, introduced by headings and the first-person plural in some canons.

key_terms.sense: Communion, both participation in the Eucharist and fellowship in the church.
Penance or repentance, the process of turning from sin and being readmitted.
Excluded from communion, excommunicated for a time.
Accursed, cut off from Christ and the church.
Heresy or sect, a false teaching or group holding it.
Catechumens, those under instruction before baptism.
Those being enlightened, i.e., candidates for baptism.
Chrism, the holy oil used for anointing after baptism.
Lent, the forty-day fast before Pascha.
The offering, the bread and wine offered in the Eucharist.
The sanctuary or altar area where only clergy may enter.
The canonical books of Scripture authorized for church reading.
Love feast, a communal meal associated with the church.
Circuit visitors appointed for rural areas instead of resident bishops.
The orarion, a liturgical vestment worn by deacons.

scripture: The council uses Greek Septuagint book names and numbering: 'Kingdoms' for Samuel-Kings, 'Paralipomenon' for Chronicles, 'Esdras' for Ezra-Nehemiah, and lists 'Jeremiah and Baruch, Lamentations and epistles' together. Modern citations should use standard English Bible names: 1-2 Samuel, 1-2 Kings, 1-2 Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah.
uncertain: The exact date of the council is uncertain; it is placed between 343 and 381.
The precise relationship between the canons and the later explanatory notes is uncertain; the notes appear to be later commentary.
The identity and status of the 'presbytides' or women elders in canon 11 is debated.
The exact meaning of 'hemiolia' in canon 4 is uncertain; it likely refers to a 50% interest rate or a particular form of interest.
The source does not state the council's location, participants, or addressee.
The source does not specify whether 'epistles' in canon 60 refers to the Epistle of Jeremiah or other letters.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Hearers: 'Those present and listening at an ordination; the source does not define them as a technical class.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Περὶ τοῦ μὴ δεῖν τὰς χειροτονίας ἐπὶ παρουσίᾳ ἀκροωμένων γίνεσθαι
_unresolved_facts.fix: The term ἀκροωμένων in canon 5 refers to 'hearers' or 'listeners' present at ordinations, but the commentary specifies they are 'ἀκροωμένους' (those listening) in contrast to the proper electors. The brief should note the commentary explicitly contrasts these hearers with the proper clergy who should conduct elections.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Ascetics: 'Those belonging to the order of ascetics, mentioned only as forbidden to enter taverns.'
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source mentions 'the order of ascetics' (τοῦ τάγματος τῶν ἀσκητῶν) in canon 24 as part of a list of those forbidden to enter taverns, but does not describe them as 'belonging to the order of ascetics' as an established class; the brief should note they appear only in this list without further definition.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Sections 14-19: 'Rules for sending the Eucharist at Pascha, who may sing and read in church, and the order of prayers in the liturgy.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Περὶ τοῦ ἐν σαββάτῳ εὐαγγέλια μετὰ ἑτέρων Γραφῶν ἀναγινώσκεσθαι
_unresolved_facts.fix: Canon 16 concerns reading Gospels with other Scriptures on Saturday, not 'who may sing and read in church.' The outline should separate canon 16 as a distinct rule about Saturday Scripture readings, not group it with liturgical personnel rules.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Sections 20-28: 'Rules on seating and duties of deacons, servants, readers, singers, exorcists, and doorkeepers, and against those in ecclesiastical orders from presbyters to ascetics entering taverns or taking portions at love feasts.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἐν τοῖς Κυριακοῖς, ἢ ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις, τὰς λεγομένας ἀγάπας ποιεῖν, ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐσθίειν, καὶ ἀκούβιτα στρωννύειν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Canon 28 forbids agapes (love feasts) in churches on Sundays, not 'taking portions at love feasts.' The brief conflates canon 27 (about taking portions at agapes, μέρη αἵρειν) with canon 28 (about holding agapes in church buildings). The outline should distinguish these: 27 is about portions at agapes, 28 is about location (not in church on Sundays).

_unresolved_facts.claim: Sections 49-52: 'Rules for Lent: no bread offerings except Saturday and Sunday, no breaking the fast on Thursday of the last week, no martyr festivals, marriages, or birthday celebrations.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἐν τῇ Τεσσαρακοστῇ τῇ ὑστέρᾳ ἑβδομάδι τὴν πέμπτην λύειν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Canon 50 forbids breaking the fast on 'the fifth [day]' (τὴν πέμπτην) in the last week of Lent, i.e., Thursday, but the brief's 'Thursday of the last week' is correct. However, canon 51 forbids 'martyr festivals' (γενέθλια) but permits 'memories' (μνήμας) of holy martyrs on Saturdays and Sundays. The brief's 'no martyr festivals' is accurate but should note the exception for Saturday/Sunday commemorations.

The source lists 'Βασιλειῶν πρώτη καὶ δευτέρα' as items 9 and 'Βασιλειῶν τρίτη καὶ τετάρτη' as item 10. The names map to: 9 = 1-2 Samuel, 10 = 1-2 Kings. The brief's mapping is correct but the source uses 'first and second of Kingdoms' as a pair (item 9), not 'the first of Kingdoms' as a separate entry. The names object should reflect the paired listing in the source.

The source lists 'Ἔσδρας πρῶτον καὶ δεύτερον' (1 and 2 Esdras), which in the Septuagint tradition typically refers to Ezra-Nehemiah as 1-2 Esdras, but the brief should note that '2 Esdras' in some traditions refers to a different apocryphal work. The mapping is generally correct for LXX usage but requires clarification.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Council of Laodicea: 'The canons are the council's own decrees, introduced by headings and the first-person plural in some canons.'
_unresolved_facts.fix: The first-person plural appears only in canons 1 (ὡρίσαμεν) and 36 (ἐκελεύσαμεν), not broadly 'in some canons' as a regular feature. Most canons use impersonal third-person constructions (ὅτι οὐ δεῖ...). The voice marking should be more precise about the limited use of first-person plural.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The canons 'require the same liturgy of prayers at the ninth hour and at vespers'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Περὶ τοῦ τὴν αὐτὴν λειτουργίαν τῶν εὐχῶν πάντοτε καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἐννάταις, καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἐσπέραις ὀφείλειν γίνεσθαι
_unresolved_facts.fix: Canon 18 states the 'same liturgy of prayers' (τὴν αὐτὴν λειτουργίαν τῶν εὐχῶν) should always be made 'at the ninth hours and at vespers' (ἐν ταῖς ἐννάταις, καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἐσπέραις). The brief's summary is accurate but should specify 'ninth hour' (not 'ninth hours') and note this refers to daily prayer offices, not the Eucharistic liturgy.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ Χριστιανοὺς ἰουδαΐζειν καὶ ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ σχολάζειν, ἀλλ᾽ ἐργάζεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἡμέρᾳ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Canon 29 forbids Christians from 'Judaizing' (ἰουδαΐζειν) specifically by resting on the Sabbath and working on Sunday, not 'Judaizing' broadly. The brief should specify the concrete practice: resting on Saturday like Jews rather than honoring Sunday.
